> OrangeOS: a cyberdeck with its own distro I'm building a cyberdeck around a Raspberry Pi 5 (16 GB kit), and since I got the priciest part for a good price, I figured: why not make my own distro for it too? I'll document the whole journey with a wiring diagram, a parts list, and config tweaks (like speeding up a slow Pi fan) you can use before flashing. I'll also write a step-by-step tutorial and keep the build cheap so anyone can make their own. Yes, I'll use AI, but to help me learn Linux and coding, not to do the work for me. OrangeOS will be as modular as possible. For example, I plan to add an ESP32 with a small screen showing temps and battery life. People will say to use an Orange Pi to match the branding, but I'm sticking with the Pi 5 since I already have it. Expect a few sleepless nights!

### 2026-10-07 – Journal: 4.5 hours installing Debian and getting the hang of it

**4.5h**

Journal: 4.5 hours installing Debian and getting the hang of it

Spent about 4.5 hours installing Debian on my Raspberry Pi 5 and learning my way around it, since this is the base I'll build OrangeOS on. I got comfortable with the terminal and how the system fits together, and spent time tinkering with the fan settings to see how much faster I can get it spinning.

I also started working out which parts I still need to continue the project. My school has a 3D printer, so I'm thinking of asking if I can use it to print a case for the cyberdeck.

Lots of trial and error, but I now have a much better feel for what I need to change for my own distro.

I will add a step by step parts list aswell and i will probably try buy some parts as i am really looking forward to a power bank which caught my attention  cuhtech 45w 20,000mah pwr bank looked small enough with the power
